cards.text: Here in Isaiah, the LORD speaks, and He opens with a short to-do list: 'Maintain justice and do what is right.' Two items, baker, TWO. I've lost longer lists than that under the takeout menus in my old junk drawer.

cards.question: Do what's right now, the LORD says, because His salvation is coming ___.

cards.text: His righteousness will be revealed too, and the man who holds it fast is BLESSED. Not 'pretty good,' not 'nice try,' but BLESSED.

cards.question: The blessed man keeps his hand from doing any evil. What else does he keep without profaning it?

cards.text: Then the passage turns to two people. First up, a foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD.

cards.question: What should the foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD not say?

answers.text: The LORD will shut me out of His people
The LORD will take away all of my land
The LORD will send me back to my country

cards.text: Next, the eunuch shouldn't say, 'I am but a dry tree.' Friend, after years in a junk drawer, I was a dry tree with a MUSTACHE.
Then the LORD Himself answers. He speaks to the eunuchs who keep His Sabbaths, choose what pleases Him and hold fast to His covenant.

cards.question: In His house and within His walls, what does the LORD give those eunuchs?

answers.text: A name better than sons and daughters
A place among the priests of Israel
A share of land for their families

cards.question: The name the LORD gives these eunuchs will last only as long as they live.

cards.text: Now back to the foreigners. The LORD speaks of the ones who join themselves to Him to minister to Him, to love His name and to be His servants.

cards.question: These foreigners also keep the Sabbath and hold fast to the LORD's covenant.
Where does the LORD say He'll bring those foreigners?
Once they're on His holy mountain, the LORD says He'll make the foreigners ___ in His house of prayer.
At the LORD's altar, the foreigners' burnt offerings and sacrifices will be turned away.
The LORD accepts their offerings, for His house will be called a house of prayer for whom?

cards.text: Then the Lord GOD, who gathers the dispersed of Israel, has one last word. Meanwhile, I've been chasing the same three sprinkles across my bakery floor since Tuesday.

cards.question: The Lord GOD says He's done gathering once Israel's scattered people are brought in.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't pass the logic test. The fact's core action is God giving a short command. The comparison's action is Papa Dorin losing lists under takeout menus. Those are different actions, so the punchline doesn't click. Calling 'Maintain justice and do what is right' a two-item to-do list also plays down the LORD's command, which leans toward making Scripture the target of the joke.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The card makes 'it' in 'holds it fast' refer to God's righteousness being revealed. In Isaiah 56:2, the blessed man is the one 'who does this,' which points back to maintaining justice and doing what is right. The card creates a link the text doesn't make and drops what the man actually does.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the exact word in the line ('joyful' versus 'silent' or 'humble'). Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason it out, so it tests wording they haven't seen rather than meaning. This matches the Psalm 23 'anoint with oil' bad example.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
